title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
authors: T. Mikolov, K. Chen, G. Corrado, J. Dean
before: Word vectors existed but training them meant running an expensive neural language model.
problem: Nobody could afford good embeddings over billions of words.
breakthrough: Strip the model to a shallow objective, predicting context from a word or vice versa. Quality vectors from 1.6 billion words in under a day.
why: Embeddings became a commodity, and the geometry of meaning became something you could inspect and reason about.
next: GloVe, then contextual embeddings from ELMo and BERT.
inherits: The vector-space view of meaning that underpins retrieval and RAG.
